newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Petrobras shares jump after sale announced.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras shares jump after sale announced.

text.p: Voting shares of Brazil's Petrobras jumped on the Sao Paulo bolsa after the federal government said it planned to sell shares in the state oil concern, brokers said on Thursday.
Petrobras common stock was up 3.57 percent at 261 reais at 1330 local/1630 GMT, traders said. A total of 35 trades, worth 2.8 million reais, were made in Petrobras common stock .

Planning Minister Antonio Kandir on Thursday confirmed that the government planned to sell 31.7 percent of Petrobras' common shares and 9.2 percent of preferred shares, bringing its stake to 51 percent of the company's voting capital.
The government has not yet set a date for the sale, Kandir said. Its only decision so far has been to transfer the excess shares to the National Privatization Fund.
Petrobras preferred, a component of the Bovespa index of the 47 most active stocks, edged 0.8 percent higher to 314.50 reais. There were 223 trades of the stock, worth 24.2 million reais.
The Bovespa index was up 1.15 percent at 11,987 points. Volume was a moderate 445.3 million reais ($412.3 million).
